scope: Reproducibility, workflow, research-object, provenance, data/version, and citation tooling. This is a source-bound technology scan, not an adoption decision, a claim of HSWM efficacy, or a replacement for HSWM-native authority, outcome, or causal-credit records.
method: Official primary documentation and official project release pages only; accessed 2026-09-13. Adoption entries report concrete institutional or implementation evidence where the primary source supplies it; they do not claim market share or general scientific prevalence.

sources.title: Workflow Run RO-Crate
sources.organization: Workflow Run RO-Crate working group / ResearchObject
sources.finding: Defines RO-Crate profiles that package a workflow execution's provenance together with inputs, outputs, code and other products; lists independent engine integrations.

sources.title: Workflow Run RO-Crate implementation table
sources.organization: Workflow Run RO-Crate working group / ResearchObject
sources.finding: Official profile page lists Galaxy, Nextflow via nf-prov, COMPSs, StreamFlow, WfExS, Sapporo and Autosubmit implementations or versioned examples; this demonstrates ecosystem use, not universal adoption.

sources.title: Common Workflow Language Standards, v1.2.1
sources.finding: Version 1.2.1 specifies command-line-tool and workflow schemas/execution semantics and publishes a runner-neutral conformance-test procedure.

sources.title: WorkflowHub project
sources.finding: Describes a FAIR, workflow-management-system-agnostic registry using RO-Crate; sponsored by EOSC-Life, ELIXIR and EU projects, with Galaxy, Nextflow and Snakemake integrations described as collaborative.

sources.title: Maintaining a registered workflow entry
sources.finding: WorkflowHub documents versioning as experimental and notes that uploaded workflow metadata and RO-Crate metadata can become out of sync; it cannot be the sole HSWM evidence authority.

sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles
sources.finding: FAIR defines Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable guidance, including persistent identifiers, rich metadata, formal shared knowledge-representation languages and qualified references. It is guidance, not a conformance standard or reproducibility proof.

sources.title: DataCite Metadata Schema 4.7
sources.finding: Current schema version is 4.7; it defines core citation/retrieval metadata and maintained controlled vocabularies, including Project, Software and relation identifiers.

sources.title: DataCite supported metadata formats
sources.finding: DataCite accepts several mapped formats, including DataCite XML/JSON, Schema.org JSON-LD, CodeMeta JSON, BibTeX, RIS and Citeproc JSON; crosswalks reduce but do not eliminate semantic mapping loss.

sources.title: Citation File Format
sources.finding: CFF 1.2.0 is YAML citation metadata for software and datasets. GitHub renders a CITATION.cff on a default branch and exposes a BibTeX snippet.

sources.title: SWHID specification v1.1
sources.finding: Defines intrinsic identifiers for software artefacts at multiple granularities without requiring a central naming authority or Software Heritage itself; archival and resolution are explicitly out of scope.

sources.title: Software Heritage SWHID documentation
sources.finding: Documents stable identifiers for archived objects and verification by recomputing the core identifier; usefulness depends on the source having been archived and on retaining qualifiers/context.

sources.title: Manage versions
sources.finding: Zenodo supports a new version of record, inheritance of prior files and browsing published versions.

sources.title: FAQ versioning
sources.finding: Zenodo cautions that DOI versioning is linear and a DOI suffix is not a general DOI-system version mechanism; release/version mapping must remain explicit in HSWM evidence.

sources.title: DVC command reference
sources.finding: DVC can retrieve data, intermediate results and models from DVC or Git repositories at a selected revision and supports remote stores.

sources.title: DVC releases
sources.finding: The official release page identifies 3.67.1 as latest and supplies a signed release commit; any adoption must pin exact package/version and remote configuration.

sources.title: MLflow Tracking
sources.finding: Tracking records parameters, code versions, metrics and output artefacts as runs and groups them into experiments; it supports local files or a shared tracking server.

sources.title: MLflow changelog
sources.finding: Changelog identifies 3.16.0 as released on 2026-09-03. This mutable main-branch changelog is discovery evidence only; an actual install must pin an immutable release artefact and digest.

sources.title: RO-Crate 1.2.0 release
sources.finding: Official release page marks RO-Crate Metadata Specification 1.2.0 as Latest, Recommendation, published 2025-06-04, and gives its immutable release tag and version permalink.

sources.title: Workflow RO-Crate profile 1.1
sources.finding: Official profile page identifies Workflow RO-Crate 1.1 and gives a compatibility table: RO-Crate 1.3 with Workflow RO-Crate 1.1; it explicitly says RO-Crate 1.2 was never formally supported by this profile.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 18670:2025 — SoftWare Hash IDentifier (SWHID) Specification V1.2
sources.finding: ISO lists Edition 1 as ISO/IEC 18670:2025, SWHID Specification V1.2, with status Published at stage 60.60. The ISO abstract says resolution is outside the standard's scope.

sources.title: Nextflow releases
sources.finding: Official releases page marks v26.04.6 Latest. Newer 26.07.0-edge and 26.08.0-edge are explicitly prereleases and are not selected as stable versions.

sources.title: nf-core institutional configuration profiles
sources.finding: Official site lists 157 institution/cluster configuration profiles, including academic and research organizations; it is concrete community deployment evidence, not a global adoption estimate.

sources.title: nf-core organizations and projects
sources.finding: Official contributor page names organizations running nf-core and describes German National Sequencing Initiative use of nf-core pipelines across national sequencing centers.

sources.title: Snakemake v9.27.0 release
sources.finding: Official release page marks v9.27.0 Latest and provides its signed release commit.

sources.title: Snakemake documentation
sources.kind: official tool documentation and project-reported adoption evidence
sources.finding: Versioned documentation identifies 9.27.0, describes portable execution across server, cluster, grid and cloud, and reports more than one million conda-forge downloads and more than 11 new citations per week; these are project-reported indicators, not independently audited prevalence.

sources.title: Galaxy v26.1.1 release
sources.finding: Official release page marks v26.1.1 Latest and supplies a signed release commit.

sources.title: Galaxy Project home
sources.finding: Official project page reports 400K+ registered users, 750K jobs per month, 22K+ citations and 150+ countries. These are project-reported service statistics, not an independently audited market measure.

sources.title: Use Galaxy
sources.finding: Official site lists 224+ Galaxy servers and identifies public servers hosted by Penn State/Johns Hopkins, Freiburg and Australian BioCommons infrastructure, alongside institutional and cloud deployments.

sources.title: Workflow Run RO-Crate Profile Collection
sources.organization: Workflow Run RO-Crate working group / ResearchObject
sources.finding: Collection defines Process Run, Workflow Run and Provenance Run profiles. Its 0.6 changelog says all three were updated on 2026-09-04 to align with RO-Crate 1.3 and Workflow RO-Crate 1.1.

sources.title: Process Run Crate 0.6
sources.organization: Workflow Run RO-Crate working group / ResearchObject
sources.finding: Profile version 0.6 extends RO-Crate 1.3 and has versioned permalink https://w3id.org/ro/wfrun/process/0.6.

sources.title: Workflow Run Crate 0.6
sources.organization: Workflow Run RO-Crate working group / ResearchObject
sources.finding: Profile version 0.6 extends Process Run Crate 0.6 and Workflow RO-Crate 1.1, and uses RO-Crate 1.3 terminology.

sources.title: Provenance Run Crate 0.6
sources.organization: Workflow Run RO-Crate working group / ResearchObject
sources.finding: Profile version 0.6 extends Workflow Run Crate 0.6 for internal step executions and intermediate outputs.

sources.title: HSWM terminal occurrence publication projection
sources.finding: Existing deterministic non-canonical export builds RO-Crate 1.3 metadata and OpenLineage RunEvent 2.0.2 START/terminal views from replay-verified SEALED or VOID terminal receipts; it excludes canonical state, Permit, causal credit and G0 passage.

sources.title: HSWM G0 occurrence-integrity profile
sources.finding: Existing profile places RO-Crate 1.3 and OpenLineage RunEvent projections after a terminal receipt and declares a valid negative/VOID terminal state publishable when its replay and artifact conditions are met.

sources.title: HSWM open connectivity contract
sources.finding: Existing synthetic typed representation rehearsal emits a projection/RDF/SHACL/PROV-O/OpenLineage/RO-Crate bundle without external service connection or operational KG publication.

candidates.name: RO-Crate
candidates.standard_status: Community-maintained open specification based on JSON-LD and Schema.org; community Recommendation, not a W3C/ISO standard.
candidates.verified_version: UNRESOLVED_OFFICIAL_SOURCE_STATUS: ResearchObject's GitHub releases page marks 1.2.0 Latest/Recommendation (2025-06-04), while the normative Workflow Run RO-Crate 0.6 collection (2026-09-04), its versioned profile pages, and existing HSWM implementation consistently reference RO-Crate 1.3. This scan cannot safely label 1.3 either released or draft from those conflicting official records.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Workflow Run RO-Crate's official implementation table names several engine integrations. Existing HSWM has deterministic RO-Crate 1.3 terminal and synthetic-rehearsal exports. Neither fact measures scientific prevalence or proves HSWM efficacy.
candidates.hswm_fit: Already implemented as an export-only, content-addressed research-package projection. It can package replay-verified terminal occurrences and synthetic representation rehearsals without becoming canonical HSWM state.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: HSWM already has source-bound JSON, RDF/N-Quads, PROV-O envelopes, hashes, receipts and RO-Crate 1.3 export code. A new packager would duplicate existing work; reuse the existing exporter and qualify it against the selected official profile/version.
candidates.qualification_needed: First resolve the normative 1.3 publication/status conflict with a direct official versioned specification record or maintain an explicit unresolved qualification. Then run profile/validator qualification against the existing exporter for (a) a preregistration/input-package rehearsal before outcome and (b) both SEALED and valid VOID terminal exports. Keep protected/private state outside public crates.
candidates.recommendation: REUSE_EXISTING_EXPORT: extend only through a source-pinned compatibility/validator qualification; publication is valid for pre-outcome package rehearsals and replay-verified negative as well as positive terminal outcomes.

candidates.name: Workflow Run RO-Crate
candidates.standard_status: Community profile collection extending RO-Crate and Schema.org; working-group specification, not a formal international standard.
candidates.verified_version: Profile collection v0.6, changelog dated 2026-09-04: Process Run Crate 0.6, Workflow Run Crate 0.6 and Provenance Run Crate 0.6. Compatibility table specifies RO-Crate 1.3 + Workflow RO-Crate 1.1 + Workflow Run profiles 0.6; RO-Crate 1.2 has no formal support.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Official table lists Galaxy, Nextflow/nf-prov, COMPSs, StreamFlow, WfExS, Sapporo and Autosubmit integration or examples. This is ecosystem implementation evidence, not a usage-rate claim.
candidates.hswm_fit: High for a portable, read-only execution-provenance package. HSWM has a lower-granularity existing RO-Crate/OpenLineage terminal projection; the profiles may be used when it needs explicit workflow/process/step semantics.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Existing HSWM terminal exporter has no declared WRROC conformance. Treating it as one would be false; WRROC can add workflow-specific fields but cannot replace HSWM replay, external-audit, authority, causal-credit or outcome contracts.
candidates.qualification_needed: Use an additive derived exporter/profile adaptor only if the selected scope needs WRROC semantics. Qualify the existing export at v0.6 against the explicit 1.3/1.1 chain, rehearse preregistration/input packages before outcomes, then test replay-verified SEALED and valid VOID terminal packages. Exclude secrets, private datasets and mutable pointers.
candidates.recommendation: TOP_CANDIDATE_AS_QUALIFICATION: reuse existing exports; add WRROC only as a version-pinned, validator-qualified profile layer when the research workflow needs it.

candidates.name: Common Workflow Language
candidates.standard_status: Community-maintained workflow standard with public versioned specification and conformance tests.
candidates.adoption_evidence: The official standard supplies a runner-neutral conformance procedure, which is stronger interoperability evidence than an engine-specific DSL claim; no broad adoption rate is asserted here.
candidates.hswm_fit: Medium for frozen batch analysis, graph validation or benchmark pipelines with ordinary command-line interfaces; low for the live HSWM Effect runtime and causal loop.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Current HSWM task and development orchestration already use typed Effect services and hswm-dev state. Translating every research process into CWL would be duplicated orchestration and may lose typed domain semantics.
candidates.qualification_needed: Choose only after one representative multi-tool batch pipeline needs engine portability. Pin runner/container/input digests and execute the official conformance suite for any selected runner.
candidates.recommendation: CONDITIONAL: use for a portable research pipeline, not as HSWM's internal runtime or graph model.

candidates.name: FAIR Guiding Principles
candidates.standard_status: Widely used guiding principles, not a tool, conformance suite or formal reproducibility standard.
candidates.verified_version: Original 2016 principles; no rolling version asserted
candidates.adoption_evidence: GO FAIR documents a stakeholder-driven implementation ecosystem. This supports institutional relevance but does not quantify uptake or certify a repository as FAIR.
candidates.hswm_fit: High as a checklist for identifiers, rich machine-readable metadata, qualified references and preservation of metadata after artefact withdrawal.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: HSWM's existing source hashes, typed references and RDF/PROV projections already cover parts of FAIR. FAIR does not specify the schema, access policy, semantics, validation or causal-learning evidence required by HSWM.
candidates.qualification_needed: Define measurable local FAIR profile checks rather than self-labeling. Record which principles each public projection meets and which are intentionally excluded for privacy or licensing.
candidates.recommendation: ADOPT_AS_CRITERIA: attach a scoped FAIR checklist to public research bundles, not a new runtime service.

candidates.name: DataCite Metadata Schema
candidates.standard_status: Consortium-maintained metadata schema used for DataCite DOI registration; not a general provenance or workflow standard.
candidates.adoption_evidence: DataCite operates a maintained schema and DOI metadata ecosystem; official documentation provides mappings to multiple common metadata formats. This is infrastructure evidence, not a guarantee that a DOI's payload is reproducible.
candidates.hswm_fit: High for final public datasets, software releases, registered workflows and project-level outputs that warrant a persistent identifier and relationship metadata.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Repository hashes and KG UIDs are internal identifiers, not public DOI metadata. DataCite cannot encode full HSWM hypergraph semantics, authority boundaries, private evidence or causal-credit decisions.
candidates.qualification_needed: Reserve DOI minting for frozen public releases. Map only declared public fields; preserve exact HSWM revision, archive DOI, license and source hash in both directions and test crosswalk loss.
candidates.recommendation: TOP_CANDIDATE_FOR_RELEASE: use through a chosen repository/registrar when an HSWM output is ready to cite.

candidates.name: Citation File Format
candidates.standard_status: Community YAML file-format specification, supported by GitHub rendering; not a formal standards-body specification.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Official CFF documentation says GitHub recognizes CITATION.cff in the default branch and renders citation/BibTeX metadata. This is a concrete platform integration, not a universal citation solution.
candidates.hswm_fit: High, low-cost repository-level citation entry point for HSWM software and a future tagged release.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: No current repository-level CFF citation record was found in the scoped scan. CFF captures credit/citation, not dependency closure, archive permanence, provenance, or empirical validity.
candidates.qualification_needed: Add only when maintainers settle release title, authorship, license and preferred citation. Validate against the published schema and cross-check the DOI against the archived release.
candidates.recommendation: TOP_CANDIDATE_LOW_COST: add at the first citable HSWM release, together with an immutable archive record.

candidates.name: Software Hash Identifier
candidates.category: intrinsic software-artifact identifier and archival reference
candidates.standard_status: ISO/IEC International Standard: ISO/IEC 18670:2025, Edition 1, SWHID Specification V1.2, published 2025-04. Software Heritage is a separate archive implementation.
candidates.verified_version: ISO/IEC 18670:2025 (SWHID Specification V1.2). The older public working-group specification v1.1 remains a distinct historical/specification source.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Software Heritage maintains the archive implementation and SWHID guidance. This is durable-archive infrastructure evidence; it does not establish that every HSWM source revision has been ingested.
candidates.hswm_fit: Medium-high for an external, intrinsic reference to a released source snapshot, complementary to Git commit IDs and archive DOIs.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: HSWM already stores SHA-256 source bindings and Git commits. SWHID adds a different object model and only helps after archive ingestion; it cannot replace source hashes, release metadata or reproducibility environments.
candidates.qualification_needed: Verify actual archive ingestion and resolve the exact qualifier-rich SWHID for a tagged release before recording it. Keep SHA-256, Git commit and SWHID distinct rather than claiming equivalence. The ISO standard explicitly leaves resolution outside its scope.
candidates.recommendation: LATER_FOR_RELEASE_ARCHIVING: add to public release provenance once an immutable source release is archived.

candidates.name: Zenodo
candidates.category: research repository and DOI publication service
candidates.standard_status: CERN-operated repository service using DOI infrastructure; not a workflow/provenance standard.
candidates.verified_version: Service documentation accessed 2026-09-13; no software version selected
candidates.adoption_evidence: Official documentation supports published version records and version browsing. That is service capability evidence, not an assertion of disciplinary usage or long-term reproducibility of every deposit.
candidates.hswm_fit: High for a frozen public release bundle, data subset, executable artefact or supplementary evidence that needs a citable DOI and version record.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Would complement Git and native receipts, not replace them. Zenodo's documented linear DOI versioning makes explicit Git tag, content hash and release manifest mandatory.
candidates.qualification_needed: Publish only licensed, non-private and reviewable material. Test a sandbox or draft-to-published flow; store exact DOI, concept DOI, record ID, files' hashes and Git tag in the KG.
candidates.recommendation: TOP_CANDIDATE_FOR_ARCHIVE: use with DataCite metadata for a frozen public research release, after an export/readback rehearsal.

candidates.name: DVC
candidates.standard_status: Independent open-source implementation, not a data/provenance standard.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Official release and documentation demonstrate active maintained software with Git- and remote-backed revision retrieval. No external adoption statistic is asserted.
candidates.hswm_fit: Medium if HSWM introduces large, mutable-but-versioned research datasets or model checkpoints that cannot live in Git and require remote-backed retrieval.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Current HSWM research evidence mainly uses Git, source pins, hashes and durable data locations. Adding DVC now would introduce a second metadata/remote state plane before a concrete large-data need is demonstrated.
candidates.qualification_needed: Pilot only on one non-sensitive, license-cleared large dataset. Pin CLI version, remote policy and lockfiles; verify a clean-machine restore and retain manifest hashes in native KG evidence.
candidates.recommendation: DEFER_UNTIL_TRIGGER: no installation or migration until a measured Git-size/restore problem occurs.

candidates.name: MLflow Tracking
candidates.standard_status: Independent open-source implementation; Databricks-associated project, not a scientific standard.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Official docs provide run/experiment models, local and shared server modes, APIs and UI. This proves maintained capability, not that its tracking semantics satisfy HSWM's causal or scientific contracts.
candidates.hswm_fit: Medium for comparing many parameterized ML/LLM runs, especially when experiment tables and artefact browsing become costly to maintain manually.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: HSWM already has source-bound KG records, CI receipts, preregistrations and restricted observability. MLflow's run log is not an authority, Permit, causal-admission or learning path and would need strict one-way projection.
candidates.qualification_needed: Do a local-only, read-only export pilot against one existing non-sensitive run. Pin version/backend/artifact URI; prove run IDs, parameter values, source commit and hashes round-trip into KG without secret leakage.
candidates.recommendation: DEFER_WITH_PILOT: useful only when repeated experiment-scale tracking exceeds the existing receipt/KG workflow.

candidates.name: Nextflow with nf-core
candidates.category: scientific workflow engine and curated pipeline community
candidates.standard_status: Nextflow and nf-core are independent open-source projects and community conventions, not formal standards. nf-core uses Nextflow and release/CI policies.
candidates.verified_version: Nextflow v26.04.6 is the official Latest stable release. v26.07.0-edge and v26.08.0-edge are prereleases and excluded. nf-core is a distributed pipeline community; no single global version applies.
candidates.adoption_evidence: nf-core officially lists 157 institutional configuration profiles and names national sequencing-center use in the German National Sequencing Initiative. This is concrete institutional deployment evidence, not a universal adoption rate.
candidates.hswm_fit: Medium for reproducible, containerized and HPC/cloud batch pipelines, particularly life-science input analyses that HSWM may invoke as bounded external research tasks.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: HSWM is not a bioinformatics pipeline suite; porting its live Effect runtime or canonical KG loop into Nextflow would duplicate orchestration and weaken typed domain semantics. A Nextflow execution receipt cannot establish HSWM causal credit or efficacy.
candidates.qualification_needed: Choose only for a concrete batch workflow with multi-environment execution needs. Pin Nextflow, all plugins, containers, Git revision, input hashes and nf-core pipeline release; export one-way provenance into existing HSWM records.
candidates.recommendation: CONDITIONAL_EXTERNAL_ENGINE: strong option for an external scientific workflow, not for the HSWM runtime or canonical state.

candidates.name: Snakemake
candidates.standard_status: Independent open-source workflow-management implementation, not a formal standard.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Official docs report more than one million conda-forge downloads and more than 11 new citations per week. These are project-reported indicators, not independently audited scientific-use totals.
candidates.hswm_fit: Medium for declarative, file-oriented analysis workflows that need local/cluster/cloud scaling and environment descriptions; useful for sealed benchmarks or reproducible data transformations.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: HSWM already uses source pins, CI, receipts and Effect typed services. Snakemake's DAG/logging does not encode HSWM relation semantics, authority, intervention design or outcome-bound learning.
candidates.qualification_needed: Pilot one existing batch analysis, pin its version and Conda/container definitions, and reproduce from a clean checkout. Preserve hidden inputs, seeds, runtime and result hashes in HSWM-native evidence instead of treating a Snakefile as complete provenance.
candidates.recommendation: CONDITIONAL_EXTERNAL_ENGINE: select when file-DAG transparency outweighs adding another workflow language.

candidates.name: Galaxy
candidates.standard_status: Independent open-source platform, not a formal workflow or provenance standard.
candidates.adoption_evidence: Galaxy's official project page reports 400K+ registered users, 750K monthly jobs, 22K+ citations and 150+ countries, and its deployment directory lists 224+ servers including Penn State/Johns Hopkins, Freiburg and Australian BioCommons. These are project-reported and service-directory figures, not independent prevalence auditing.
candidates.hswm_fit: Low-medium for HSWM core work; high only where an accessible UI and established bioinformatics tools/workflows are needed for a bounded research dataset pipeline.
candidates.cost_or_overlap: Galaxy tracks analysis history/provenance but is a full platform with its own user, data and workflow state. It must remain an external evidence-producing surface and must not become an HSWM canonical-write, Permit or learning path.
candidates.qualification_needed: Use a public/sandbox or isolated deployment first, document exact server/version/tool versions/history export, and evaluate privacy/licensing. Bind Galaxy exports to HSWM source hashes and immutable result artefacts.
candidates.recommendation: SPECIALIZED_EXTERNAL_OPTION: use for domain-specific interactive analyses, not as general HSWM workflow infrastructure.
